newsitem.title: FRANCE: Fire hits masonic groups in French far-right town.
newsitem.headline: Fire hits masonic groups in French far-right town.

text.p: - A fire damaged a building housing five masonic associations in Orange, one of three French towns controlled by the far-right National Front, and investigators suspect arson, police sources said on Tuesday.
"The fire seems to have been arson. A window was broken and a bottle of white spirit was discovered inside," the sources said.
Leaders of the local masonic groups implied in a statement that the blaze, which started late on Monday in the municipally-owned building, was the work of extreme-rightists.
"It is clear that the political climate in Orange can only incite such acts," it said.

"By its unflinching attachment to republican values, the (Freemason leadership) has made itself a natural adversary of the ideas of the extreme right in general, and of the municipality of Orange in particular," it said.
There was no immediate comment from the National Front.
Masons, Jews and Communists are traditional targets of the National Front leader Jean-Marie Le Pen's rhetoric.
